sections.label: Singaporeans aged 65 and above
sections.summary: More than 450,000 Singaporeans are 65 and above, and by 2030 one in four will be 65 and above, over 900,000 elderly individuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Today, more than 450,000 Singaporeans are 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In 12 years, by 2030, one in four will be aged 65 and above; that is more than 900,000 elderly individuals.

sections.label: Adult Protective Service referrals
sections.summary: Since APS was established in 2015, referrals to MSF have increased, with about 110 cases annually involving vulnerable adults 18 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Since MSF’s Adult Protective Service (APS) was established in 2015, the number of referrals to MSF has increased.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: On average, we have handled about 110 cases annually involving vulnerable adults 18 years and above, though not all of these cases eventually required our intervention.

sections.label: Bill as law of last resort
sections.summary: Social work intervention remains the main external intervention, and the Bill should be a law of last resort applied judiciously and only when necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Social work intervention is, and remains, the main form of external intervention in such cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This Bill, if passed by Members, should be a law of last resort; state intervention through the exercise of statutory power into the family for family matters will be applied judiciously and only when necessary.

sections.label: Definition of vulnerable adult
sections.summary: Clause 2 defines a vulnerable adult as an individual 18 or older incapable of protecting himself from abuse, neglect or self-neglect due to infirmity, disability or incapacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Clause 2 of the Bill defines a vulnerable adult as an individual, aged 18 or older, who because of mental or physical infirmity, disability or incapacity, is incapable of protecting himself from abuse, neglect or self-neglect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For individuals above the age of 16 but below 18, we are looking to amend the Children and Young Persons Act (CYPA) to extend statutory protection under the realm of the Child Protective Services, which is the sister agency of the Adult Protection Service (APS).

sections.label: APS self-neglect cases
sections.summary: Since 2015, APS has seen close to 50 cases of self-neglect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Since 2015, APS has seen close to 50 cases of such self-neglect.

sections.label: Need for adult protection legislation
sections.summary: Cases like Mr Wong's highlight the need for adult protection legislation giving Government social services powers to better support vulnerable adults.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Cases like Mr Wong's highlight the need for adult protection legislation that will provide Government social services with powers to better support these vulnerable adults.

sections.label: MSF powers to intervene
sections.summary: Part 2 Division 1 empowers MSF to enter premises, assess suspected vulnerable adults, and remove them, requiring a Court order within 14 working days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Bill will only be effective if it allows us to intervene quickly to prevent further harm to the vulnerable adult.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, Part 2, Division 1 of the Bill empowers MSF to enter private premises, to assess a person whom we suspect to be a vulnerable adult, if we have reason to believe that the individual has suffered from, is suffering or is at risk of abuse, neglect or self-neglect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Under clauses 10 and 11, MSF may remove vulnerable adults from their residence and commit them to gazetted care facilities, or to the care of a fit person.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: MSF must apply for a Court order within 14 working days after the removal, unless the vulnerable adult is earlier permitted to return to his residence.

sections.label: Court order despite refusal
sections.summary: Clauses 7 and 10 let MSF apply for a Court order to assess and commit a vulnerable adult with mental capacity who refuses assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Clauses 7 and 10 will, therefore, allow MSF to apply for a Court order to assess and commit a vulnerable adult to a care facility, where a vulnerable adult with mental capacity refuses assistance.

sections.label: Investigations and enhanced penalties
sections.summary: Clauses 26 to 29 empower MSF to investigate offences, and clauses 40 and 41 enhance maximum penalties for offences against vulnerable adults.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Clauses 26 to 29 empower MSF to investigate offences under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And to deter people from harming vulnerable adults, clauses 40 and 41 make related amendments to the Penal Code and Protection of Harassment Act respectively to enhance the maximum penalties of specific offences by up to one and a half times if these acts are committed against the vulnerable adult.

sections.label: Family Justice Courts intervention orders
sections.summary: Clause 14 empowers the Family Justice Courts to make intervention orders protecting vulnerable adults from further harm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Clause 14 empowers the Family Justice Courts to make intervention orders to protect vulnerable adults from further harm.

sections.label: Sam placed in care facility
sections.summary: The Bill, if supported, will allow Sam to be placed in a care facility to manage his condition and recover from physical abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Bill, if Members support it, will allow Sam to be placed in a care facility, where he will receive the support necessary for him to manage his condition and recover from physical abuse.

sections.label: Protection for reporters
sections.summary: Clause 23 protects people who report such cases to the relevant authorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Specifically, clause 23 protects people who report such cases to the relevant authorities.

sections.label: Vulnerable adult information restrictions
sections.summary: Clause 22 restricts publication of identifying information to protect a vulnerable adult's privacy, while clause 24 allows disclosure to MSF and other bodies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Clause 22 also places restrictions on the publication of information identifying a vulnerable adult.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This is to safeguard a vulnerable adult's privacy and allow him to recover; this privacy will also allow the vulnerable adult and the family to focus on repairing their relationship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: That said, clause 24 allows the disclosure of confidential information relating to a vulnerable adult to MSF, and by us to any other Government agency, statutory body, Police Officer or prescribed person or body.

sections.label: Legal liability protection for helpers
sections.summary: Clause 34 protects anyone performing functions under the Vulnerable Adults Bill from legal liability if they acted in good faith and with reasonable care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: If we want those who work with vulnerable adults to carry out their duties diligently and professionally, we must provide them peace of mind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, clause 34 protects anyone performing a function or exercising powers under the Vulnerable Adults Bill from legal liability, so long they have acted in good faith and with reasonable care.

sections.label: MSF community outreach networks
sections.summary: MSF will reinforce existing help networks and work with families, professionals and volunteers to reach vulnerable adults and their caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Beyond the Bill, MSF will continue to facilitate the community's efforts in reaching out to vulnerable adults.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will reinforce our existing help networks, such as our Social Service Offices' local networks and the Community Network for Seniors programme, to better reach out to vulnerable adults and their caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Even as we operationalise the Bill, we will continue to work with families, professionals and volunteers to strengthen the care networks across the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Together, we can all do our part to keep an eye out for the most vulnerable members of our society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This is a Bill that has been in the making for a long time and aims to protect vulnerable adults in our midst from abuse and neglect.

sections.label: Bill complementing existing legislation
sections.summary: The Vulnerable Adults Bill will provide a final safeguard, and the Minister is asked how it complements existing Adult Protective Services and legislation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: With the rapidly increasing numbers of elderly Singaporeans, the number of persons diagnosed with special needs, and the increasing number of persons with mental illnesses in a highly urbanised society like ours, the Vulnerable Adults Bill will provide the final safeguard to protect persons, such as them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As there is a current slew of many legislation and services which covers the same target group of vulnerable adults that the Minister has mentioned, can the Minister explain how the proposed Bill will complement exactly at the operational level existing Adult Protective Services and legislation, such as the Mental Capacity Act and the Women's Charter?

sections.label: Adult Protective Services case numbers
sections.summary: About 250 cases were identified by the Adult Protective Services, largely involving adults with intellectual and physical disabilities, psychiatric conditions and illnesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Since the formation of the Adult Protective Services by the Ministry, I understand from somewhere I read that the data is that about 250 cases were identified, largely involving adults with intellectual and physical disabilities, psychiatric conditions and illnesses.

sections.label: John's death from fall
sections.summary: John's life ended prematurely when he fell to his death, reportedly trying to climb out of the flat he was locked in.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: John's life was prematurely ended when he fell to his death, reportedly trying to climb out of the flat he was locked in.

sections.label: Daycare, volunteers and community support
sections.summary: A Centre and its volunteers gave a man in his 30s daily daycare, and his brother could volunteer after work because of the respite.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Centre and many of its volunteers then offered him daily daycare services even though he was only in his 30s when we found him and not exactly a senior citizen.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: His brother could even become a volunteer after work because of this respite that he now gets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I share this tale of the two men to highlight the usefulness of the Vulnerable Adults Bill in the case of John; and the importance of community support in the case of Er Ge.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Unless we seriously organise and harness the potential of the community around them, these adults will not be found nor liberated.

sections.label: Clause 4 powers and concerns
sections.summary: Clause 4 requires respect and self-determination for vulnerable adults, and the speaker asks about division of work, assessment rigour and definitions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 4 provides that in exercising any of the powers under the Bill, a vulnerable adult must be respected and have the right of self-determination and not be subject to any unnecessary restrictions on his rights and freedom of action.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, what will be the division of work between the Ministry under this Bill and the Office of the Public Guardian?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, what is the rigour of assessment to be applied before the state decides to intervene to change a person's living arrangements?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am worried about possible Government overreach, causing unnecessary institutionalisation of vulnerable adults, which, itself, would have harmful effects.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, would the definitions of "abuse", "neglect" and "self-neglect" in the Bill inadvertently discriminate against the poor?

sections.label: Clause 2 abuse definition
sections.summary: Clause 2 states a vulnerable adult may be considered abused if subject to physical, emotional or psychological abuse, domination or unreasonable deprivation of liberty.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to clause 2, a vulnerable adult may be considered to be abused if he is subject to physical, emotional or psychological abuse, is subject to domination or has been unreasonably deprived of liberty of movement or well-being.

sections.label: Case-by-case assessment before intervention
sections.summary: The speaker expects a case-by-case and subjective assessment before the state exercises its drastic powers of intervention.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Before the state exercises its drastic powers of intervention, I would expect that a case-by-case and subjective assessment would have to be made.

sections.label: Deputyship costs for small balances
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether deputyship can be streamlined and made cost-effective when legal fees exceed small balances like $5,000 or $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With small balances like, say, $5,000 or $10,000, it does not make sense for family members to fork out, say, $6,000 in legal fees to apply to Court to be appointed deputies, especially when the money has to be paid upfront by them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Government look into how the process of deputyship in such cases can also be streamlined and made cost-effective?

sections.label: Judicious use of Bill powers
sections.summary: The Bill's powers need judicious use to avoid Government overreach and unnecessary separation, and the Bill seeks to safeguard vulnerable adults from abuse, neglect or self-neglect.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As mentioned earlier, the powers given in the Bill need to be judiciously used, so as not to result in Government overreach and unnecessary separation of vulnerable adults from their family and home settings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There is also room for improvement to give vulnerable adults the assurance that society as a whole understands their plight and sees them as integral members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Vulnerable Adults Bill seeks to safeguard vulnerable adults from abuse, neglect or self-neglect.

sections.label: Director empowered to protect vulnerable persons
sections.summary: Section 34 notwithstanding, clarity on protection scope and adherence to section 4 principles will empower the Director and others to act boldly to protect the vulnerable person.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Despite section 34, clarity on the scope of protection and a strong adherence to the principles set out in section 4, will empower the Director and such other persons to act boldly and courageously to protect the vulnerable person.

sections.label: Emotional abuse and neglect definitions
sections.summary: The speaker says it is left open whether non-action such as indifference or inaction in treatment is emotional or psychological abuse, and defines neglect.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When I read the definition of "emotional or psychological abuse", together with the illustrations, I believe, Sir, that the question is left open as to whether non-action, such as indifference or just complete inaction in treatment constitutes emotional or psychological abuse.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I move on to the definition of "Neglect".

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It means the lack of provision to the individual of essential care, to the extent of causing or being reasonably likely to cause personal injury or physical pain to, or injury to the mental or physical health of, the individual.

sections.label: Proposal to replace means with includes
sections.summary: The speaker proposes the Minister consider amending the three definitions by replacing "means" with "includes".

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At this point, I would like to propose that the Minister consider amending the three definitions by replacing "means" with the word "includes".

sections.label: Conditions for self-neglect requirement
sections.summary: Self-neglect requires the individual's failure to care for himself or herself to result in unsanitary or hazardous living conditions, malnutrition or dehydration, or untreated illness or injury.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In order for the requirement of "self-neglect" to be fulfilled, the failure of the individual to care for himself or herself must result in the individual: (a) living in grossly unsanitary or hazardous conditions; (b) suffering from malnutrition or dehydration; or (c) suffering from an untreated physical or mental illness or injury.

sections.label: Proposal to delete grossly
sections.summary: The speaker proposes that the word "grossly" be deleted from (i) of the definition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition, I would also propose that the word "grossly" be deleted from (i) of the definition.

sections.label: Court order for removal refusal
sections.summary: An order of Court is required where a vulnerable adult with mental capacity refuses consent for his or her removal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, it also requires an order of Court where a vulnerable adult, notwithstanding possessing mental capacity, refuses to give consent for his or her removal.

sections.label: Court order for assessment
sections.summary: The Director must satisfy the Court of abuse, neglect or self-neglect risk and that an assessment order is necessary for safety and protection.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, the Director must (a)	satisfy the Court that, on a balance of probabilities, the individual or vulnerable adult has experienced, or is experiencing or is at risk of, abuse, neglect or self-neglect; and (b)	persuade the Court that such an order for assessment is necessary for the safety and protection of the individual or vulnerable adult.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If the Director is able to satisfy both requirements, should he not be empowered, in the first instance, to remove the vulnerable adult for the protection of the vulnerable adult?

sections.label: Proposed amendments and reporting
sections.summary: The speaker proposes amendments, asks the Minister to consider facilities and exclusion powers, and urges neighbours to report abuse.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Section 7(1) provides that the Director is not required to exercise any power under section 6 if consent is refused by the vulnerable adult with mental capacity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: As such, I would propose the amendments that I have suggested, and I would also like to ask that the Minister consider other amendments; consider provision of facilities to cater to the needs of vulnerable adults.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: I also ask that we not be shy to exercise and to apply for powers of exclusion of the abusers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: The case of Annie Ee and other unfortunate cases tell us that there will be many out there in the community who would have fallen through the gaps.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: They have, in some cases, played a critical role in saving someone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: So, I urge neighbours, it is better to report to save a life or even a family, than to report to retrieve a body.

sections.label: Financial abuse legal gap
sections.summary: A 2014 Trans Family survey found 29% of elderly mistreatment involves financial exploitation, and the legal framework has gaps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A 2014 survey conducted by Trans Family found that 29% of elderly mistreatment in Singapore involves financial exploitation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: There appears to be a gap in the current legal framework for addressing financial abuse and exploitation of vulnerable adults.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For instance, finance-related offences under the Penal Code, such as theft, extortion and cheating, may not be sufficiently nuanced to address financial exploitation in the context of an existing relationship of trust or dependency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Protection orders under the Women's Charter does not extend to financial abuse.

sections.label: Police reporting and reintegration
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether all abuse cases are reported to Police, how the Mental Health Act provision operates, and about reintegration plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will every case of vulnerable adult abuse be reported to the Police?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: There is an existing mechanism under section 8 of the Mental Health (Care and Treatment) Act that allows a Magistrate to investigate a report from any person or Police Officer that a mentally disordered person is not under proper care and control or is ill-treated or neglected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify how this provision will operate in relation to the Bill?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Lastly, can the Minister also share the plans for ensuring successful reintegration and adequate care of vulnerable adults when they are returned to their homes from place of temporary care and protection?

sections.label: Elderly living alone increase
sections.summary: By 2030 over 900,000 residents will be aged 65 and above, with those living alone rising from 31,200 in 2012 to 83,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: By 2030, over 900,000 residents in Singapore will be aged 65 and above, and an increasing number will be living alone, from 31,200 in 2012 to 83,000 in 2030.

sections.label: Powers and mandatory reporting
sections.summary: Mental capacity assessments and entry and removal powers can be enforced, and the speaker suggests a mandatory reporting system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Assessments of mental capacity can be enforced, the power of entering a vulnerable adult's premises can be exercised and, most importantly, there is a power to remove the vulnerable adult from the premises and to a safer place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: My first suggestion is to implement a mandatory reporting system for all stakeholders involved in providing care and services for vulnerable adults.

sections.label: Financial abuse of vulnerable adults
sections.summary: A suggestion is made to consider including financial abuse of vulnerable adults under the Bill's ambit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: My second suggestion is to consider including financial abuse of vulnerable adults under the ambit of this Bill.

sections.label: Bill's current abuse types
sections.summary: The proposed Bill currently includes only physical, sexual or emotional/psychological abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: As it currently stands, the proposed Bill only includes physical, sexual or emotional/psychological abuse.

sections.label: Financial exploitation definition inclusion
sections.summary: A 2014 study found one-in-three elder abuse cases involved financial abuse, and including financial exploitation in the definition is suggested.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In fact, one-in-three cases of elder abuse involved financial abuse as well, according to a 2014 study by Trans Safe Centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Including "financial exploitation" under the definition of "abuse" in the Bill would, I believe, be a good starting point in securing the financial interests of vulnerable adults.

sections.label: Costs of intervention
sections.summary: A clarification is raised on who bears the costs of intervention under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: As some points of clarification, this pertains to the issue of cost: who bears the costs of intervention under the Bill?

sections.label: Reported abuse cases annually
sections.summary: About 200 reported cases of abuse of seniors and people with disabilities occur yearly, which is reason for the Bill's urgency.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Every year, we see about 200 reported cases of abuse of seniors and people with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is sufficient reason, in itself, for the urgency of the Bill.

sections.label: Gaps in protection and definition
sections.summary: Young persons aged 16 to 17 lack protection, and the abuse definition excludes financial abuse of vulnerable adults' resources.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Our young persons aged between 16 and 17 are left in no-man’s-land in terms of protection from abuse or neglect.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The second gap is that the definition of abuse does not include financial abuse when the vulnerable adults' resources are being exploited by perpetrators for their financial gain or personal benefit.

sections.label: MSF protectors and intervention powers
sections.summary: The speaker says Police and the Office of Public Guardian are less equipped than MSF protectors to investigate financial abuse, and argues some powers should be intermediate.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: With all due respect to the abilities of the Police and the Office of Public Guardian, they are not as well-equipped as the MSF protectors and the powers under the Bill to investigate, detect and assess incidents of financial abuse.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The second point I would like to raise for the Bill is that while the statutory powers of intervention should generally be deemed as powers of last resort compared to the family and community interventions, there is scope and justification for some of the powers to be deemed as intermediate powers.

sections.label: Charges needed to suspend donee
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether evidence would suffice for fraud charges and whether the process is quick enough, since the Office of Public Guardian can apply to Court only if the donee or deputy is charged.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would the evidence be sufficient to bring charges against the perpetrators for fraud or dishonesty offences and the process be quick enough to stop the harm being done to the vulnerable adult?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I am asking this because the Office of Public Guardian can only apply to Court to suspend the powers of the donee or deputy if the donee or deputy has been charged for a financial offence.

sections.label: PPO applications and Bill support
sections.summary: The speaker suggests allowing immediate family members and selected agencies to apply for PPOs on victims' behalf, and supports the Bill while noting its human dignity issues.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: One compromise could be for the law to be amended to allow immediate family members of victims of family violence and perhaps selected social service agencies, the Police and MSF protectors included, to apply for PPOs on behalf of victims.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, I believe the Bill would become a landmark law in our legislative history.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It has far greater ramifications and the express intentions to keep abuse rates low in an ageing society.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In fact, the Bill has raised, and the Act will continue to raise, many issues regarding human dignity and human rights and the role the state plays to protect and provide for the more vulnerable members of our society.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Already a number of cases of abuse of neglect and self-neglect have made headlines recently and sparked intense discussions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, I support the Bill and look forward to tracking closely the effectiveness of its implementation on the ground.

sections.label: Staying in touch and LPAs
sections.summary: The speaker proposes better contact with vulnerable adults before crisis and minimising vulnerable adults through Lasting Power of Attorneys for mental incapacitation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Today, I would like to propose two things: how we can better stay in touch with vulnerable adults prior to a crisis which requires intervention; and how we can minimise the number of vulnerable adults through the Lasting Power of Attorneys (LPAs), by getting as many Singaporeans as possible to predetermine their caregiving arrangements in the event of a mental incapacitation.

sections.label: ICA inserting LPA process
sections.summary: The speaker suggests ICA insert the LPA process automatically within identity card re-registration at 55 and passport renewal for Singaporeans over 45.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) can insert the LPA process automatically within the 55-year-old identity card re-registration process as well as passport renewal for Singaporeans over 45 years old.

sections.label: Default LPA in Mental Capacity Act
sections.summary: The speaker proposes revising the Mental Capacity Act to include a default LPA that automatically determines the right person to take charge absent a voluntary LPA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The other way is to revise our Mental Capacity Act to include a "default LPA".

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: By "default LPA", it means having the law to automatically determine the right person to take charge, in the absence of an LPA made voluntarily.

sections.label: Default LPA and care costs
sections.summary: Suggests guidelines on reasonable care costs and that the RERF Committee explore the default LPA issue, while pushing mass adoption of voluntary LPAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This could include clear guidelines on what constitutes reasonable cost for medical and long-term care of the donors and caregiving of the donor's direct dependants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I understand that Minister Desmond Lee has set up the Committee to Review and Enhance Reforms in the Family Justice System (RERF) recently to review family law issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Perhaps, the Committee can take the lead to explore the default LPA issue very carefully in consultation with the lawyers, the legal community and the people sector, so that we can have at least one additional option to minimise the number of vulnerable adults.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But, of course, the first logical no-regrets move we should do is to push for the mass adoption of voluntary LPAs.

sections.label: Minimising vulnerable seniors via LPAs
sections.summary: Hopes focus stays on minimising vulnerable seniors, partly by getting all Singaporeans to write up their LPAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Moving forward, I also hope we can focus on the urgent task of minimising the number of vulnerable seniors, and one good way is to get all Singaporeans to write up their LPAs.

sections.label: Age 18 and persons aged 14 to 17
sections.summary: Asks how the age of 18 was decided and how vulnerable persons aged 14 to 17 are supported.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: An "adult" is defined as 21 years of age in the majority of Singapore's laws.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How has the age of 18 been decided in this Bill?

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As the Children and Young Persons Act covers children below age 14, and this Bill covers persons from 18 and above, how would the vulnerable persons between ages 14 and 17 that are not covered under this Bill be supported?

sections.label: Responsibility for care costs
sections.summary: Asks who would be responsible for the cost of care and other costs such as necessary medical attention.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Who would be responsible for the cost of care and any other costs, such as those requiring medical attention deemed necessary by professionals?

sections.label: Admitting recorded voice or video evidence
sections.summary: Suggests the Court allow Police voice recordings, or video with blurred faces, without disclosing names or addresses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: One solution would be for the Court to allow voice evidence recorded by Police as admissible in Court, without disclosing the names/addresses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Or it could be a video recording, but the face of the witness be blurred out to protect the identity of the witness.

sections.label: Extending ComCare hotline scope
sections.summary: Proposes the visible ComCare hotline extend its scope to help families find the right organisation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The ComCare hotline is very visible to residents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I propose that this hotline extends its scope to help families to point them to the right organisation.

sections.label: Family circumstances in MSF intervention
sections.summary: The speaker hopes MSF will weigh family circumstances so intervention does not break up family ties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And worse, the vulnerable adult is abused because the family is unable to find a solution to care for him/her.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I hope that in cases where MSF has to intervene, it will weigh the family's circumstances so that the action taken will not result in the breaking up of family ties.

sections.label: Bill omits financial abuse
sections.summary: The Bill does not cover financial abuse, which a 2014 study found affected about one in three seniors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I am glad most of these are now covered in this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: However, this Bill does not cover financial abuse, as mentioned by other Parliamentarians earlier.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As mentioned by my Parliamentary colleague Mr Seah Kian Peng earlier, a 2014 study by Trans Safe Centre, a charity that specialises in tackling elder abuse, showed that about one in three involved a senior who had been financially abused.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: With each passing year, the growing numbers of seniors will reach 900,000 by 2030.

sections.label: Publicity and whistleblower protection
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes Part 4 of clause 23, which protects whistleblowers who report abused or neglected cases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Publicity and raising awareness on this topic and information on the kind of assistance available are thus very important.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I welcome Part 4 of clause 23, which provides protection to whistleblowers for providing the information on abused or neglected cases.

sections.label: Assessments and assessor availability
sections.summary: Clauses 5 and 6 empower the Director or a protector to have an individual or vulnerable adult assessed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Under Part 2, clauses 5 and 6, this Bill empowers the Director or a protector to assess an individual or a vulnerable adult to be assessed by a qualified assessor.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Every assessment can only be complete with both physical and mental well-being taken together.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Will these assessors be at hand on the enactment of this Bill?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Areas of priority are good publicity, getting the buy-in from the community and enough personnel that will carry out their duties diligently.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As we intensify our efforts in being more inclusive and providing for the less fortunate and the vulnerable, this Bill is timely which seeks to provide for the safeguard of vulnerable adults from abuse, neglect or self-neglect.

sections.label: Framework for vulnerable adults
sections.summary: The speaker says a better framework and set of laws is needed to provide for vulnerable adults.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These are the vulnerable adults who live amongst us.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: There needs to be a better framework and set of laws to manage how we are able to provide for them and ensure their well-being and safety, as well as that of others around them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While I generally support the intents of this Bill, there are some clauses within the Bill which I seek clarifications on.

sections.label: Force to remove vulnerable adult
sections.summary: Under clause 10(5), the Director or protector may use force considered necessary to remove the vulnerable adult.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Third, for clause 10(5), the Director or protector may use such force considered necessary to remove the vulnerable adult.

sections.label: Vulnerable adults intervention sensitivities
sections.summary: The passage states there are many causes and levers for intervention in vulnerable adult cases and many sensitivities in balancing state intervention with individual rights and choices.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While there are many causes and levers for intervention in the case of vulnerable adults among us, there are equally as many sensitivities in calibrating the balance between state intervention and individual rights and choices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: As my other colleagues have said, this has been a long-awaited Bill, with many hoping to see more teeth in legislation to help safeguard vulnerable adults from abuse, neglect or self-neglect.

sections.label: Assessor requirements and care capacity
sections.summary: The passage asks about assessor requirements, specified training, and sufficient manpower, support and care facilities for seamless care of vulnerable adults.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: What would be the requirements of these assessors and would there be specified training given to them?

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Do we have sufficient manpower, support and spaces like the care facilities that the Minister referred to, to ensure that the care of these vulnerable adults, temporary or otherwise, is seamless and comprehensive?

sections.label: Officer training and equipment
sections.summary: The passage asks whether all officers are fully trained and equipped to handle various circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Are all our officers fully trained and equipped to handle various circumstances?

sections.label: Do-gooders reporting family violence
sections.summary: The passage states that last year one in three hotline callers reporting family violence were do-gooders, up from one in five before the campaign.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Last year, one in three callers to our hotline who reported family violence matters were do-gooders, such as neighbours, friends and passers-by.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This is an increase from one in five, prior to the campaign.

sections.label: Mandatory reporting decision reasons
sections.summary: The passage states Mr Seah Kian Peng suggested mandatory reporting for stakeholders interacting with suspected vulnerable adults, but it was decided against for now for two reasons, including overseas over-reporting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Mr Seah Kian Peng suggested implementing a mandatory reporting system for stakeholders who interact with suspected vulnerable adults.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But we decided against it for now for two reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Second, we understand that mandatory reporting laws in overseas jurisdictions have led to over-reporting, many of which were also unsubstantiated.

sections.label: Personal protection order application
sections.summary: The passage states a personal protection order may be applied for under that Act on behalf of the vulnerable person.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: A personal protection order (PPO) may be applied for under that Act on behalf of the vulnerable person.

sections.label: Suspending donee or deputy powers
sections.summary: The Public Guardian may seek a Court order to suspend or revoke a donee's or deputy's powers to prevent further abuse of a vulnerable adult lacking mental capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, the family can take action to resolve financial abuse within their own families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But in cases where the vulnerable adult lacks mental capacity and the alleged abuser is a donee appointed under an LPA or a deputy appointed by the Court, the Public Guardian may seek a Court order to suspend or revoke his powers to make decisions on the vulnerable adult's behalf, to prevent further abuse.

sections.label: Professional Deputies and Donees Scheme
sections.summary: Under the upcoming Professional Deputies and Donees Scheme, commencing in the second half of this year, the Courts can appoint a professional deputy to step in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Under our upcoming Professional Deputies and Donees Scheme which will commence in the second half of this year, a professional deputy can be appointed by the Courts to step in.

sections.label: Vulnerable Adults Bill abuse focus
sections.summary: The Police will investigate suspected offences, and the Vulnerable Adults Bill currently focuses on physical and emotional abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: If there is suspicion that offences have been committed, and the Police will also investigate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, for now, the Vulnerable Adults Bill's focus is on physical and emotional abuse.

sections.label: Protectors in MSF APS
sections.summary: Protectors will be senior MSF APS officers with suitable qualifications and experience to handle vulnerable adult abuse, neglect and self-neglect cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Protectors will be our senior officers in MSF's APS who have suitable qualifications and experience to handle vulnerable adult abuse, neglect and self-neglect cases.

sections.label: Enhancing caregiver skills before removal
sections.summary: Where a willing but unskilled caregiver exists, we help enhance caregiver skills instead of removing the vulnerable adult, invoking removal only when safety is compromised or at risk, and never for lack of family financial means.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Where a caregiver is willing and able to look after the vulnerable adult but lacks the skills to provide adequate support, we will help him enhance his caregiver skills, instead of removing the vulnerable adult.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will invoke removal only when the vulnerable adult's safety and well-being have been compromised or are at risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Neither will we remove a vulnerable adult because his family members do not have financial means to provide care.

sections.label: Balancing concerns and vulnerable adult's interest
sections.summary: Both concerns are valid and we want to strike the right balance, avoiding overreach while ensuring the vulnerable adult's interest is first and paramount, as enshrined in clause 4.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In fact, both are valid concerns and we want to strike the right balance, avoiding overreach while ensuring that the first and paramount interest is that of the vulnerable adult, as enshrined in clause 4 of the Bill.

sections.label: Court order for intervention
sections.summary: MSF can intervene only after a Court order has been obtained where the need arises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, where the need arises, MSF has built in a safeguard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We can only intervene in such a situation after a Court order has been obtained.

sections.label: Gazetting residential care facilities
sections.summary: Some existing residential care facilities will be gazetted as places of temporary care and protection and places of safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Some existing residential care facilities, such as some of the adult disability homes and sheltered homes, will be gazetted as places of temporary care and protection and places of safety.

sections.label: Interim stay in protection places
sections.summary: Places of temporary care and protection house vulnerable adults for an interim period, generally not longer than six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: However, places of temporary care and protection are only meant to house vulnerable adults for an interim period, so that investigations can be carried out and longer-term care plans made.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Therefore, the length of stay in these premises will generally not be longer than six months.

sections.label: Court order against perpetrator
sections.summary: A Court may issue an order preventing an alleged perpetrator of abuse or neglect from visiting or contacting the vulnerable adult.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For instance, a Court may issue an order preventing the alleged perpetrator of abuse or neglect from visiting or contacting the vulnerable adult.

sections.label: Families responsible for vulnerable members
sections.summary: Families are primarily responsible to provide for their vulnerable members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Families are primarily responsible to provide for their vulnerable members.

sections.label: State pays temporary placement costs
sections.summary: The state will pay for temporary placement in gazetted care facilities and related costs, and will engage vulnerable adults and families on home care plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In such instances, the state will pay for the temporary placement of these individuals in gazetted care facilities and related costs that may be incurred to ensure the vulnerable adult’s well-being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It is not ideal for a vulnerable adult to stay in a care facility for the long term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will engage both the vulnerable adults and their families to establish safety and care plans at home.

sections.label: Limiting deputy and donee powers
sections.summary: MSF has sought to limit a deputy's or donee's powers to consent or refuse treatment for the vulnerable adult under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: MSF has sought to limit a deputy’s or donee’s powers to consent or refuse treatment for the vulnerable adult under the Bill, as there may be situations where the donee or deputy cannot be contacted in time, or – and this is pertinent – the donee or deputy is the abuser of the vulnerable adult and, thus, out of fear or some other reason, may refuse to give consent to treatment.

sections.label: Vulnerable Adults Bill and Women's Charter
sections.summary: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh asked about the interface between the Vulnerable Adults Bill and the Women's Charter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh asked about the interface between the Vulnerable Adults Bill and the Women’s Charter.

sections.label: Bill invoked for victims
sections.summary: The Bill will be invoked as these victims may no longer be able to protect themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Bill will be invoked as these victims may no longer be able to protect themselves.

sections.label: Caregivers Training Grant
sections.summary: The Caregivers Training Grant supports caregivers, including foreign domestic workers, to enhance their caregiving skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Third, the Caregivers Training Grant supports caregivers, including foreign domestic workers, to enhance their caregiving skills.

sections.label: Strengthening Social Service Offices
sections.summary: As part of SG Cares, MSF will strengthen the role and capabilities of Social Service Offices over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: First, as part of SG Cares, MSF will strengthen the role and capabilities of our Social Service Offices (SSOs) over the next five years.

sections.label: Community Network for Seniors
sections.summary: MOH will expand the Community Network for Seniors island-wide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Fourth, MOH will expand the Community Network for Seniors island-wide.

sections.label: Active Ageing Hubs expansion
sections.summary: MOH expanded senior care centres into Active Ageing Hubs providing day care and rehabilitation to frail seniors and engaging healthy seniors in active ageing programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: MOH has also expanded senior care centres into Active Ageing Hubs (AAHs) which not only provide day care and day rehabilitation to frail seniors but also seek to engage seniors who are healthy in active ageing programmes.

sections.label: Universal adoption of LPAs
sections.summary: One key objective is moving towards universal adoption of LPAs in a citizen-centric yet efficient manner using a life stage approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: One key objective is to see how we can move towards universal adoption of LPAs in a citizen-centric yet efficient manner and adopting a life stage approach.

sections.label: Simplifying deputyship applications
sections.summary: One assigned task is to see how deputyship applications can be made simpler, more affordable and accessible, especially for straightforward and uncontested cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: One of the tasks that we have assigned them is to see how the deputyship application can be made simpler, more affordable and accessible, especially for straightforward and uncontested cases.

sections.label: CYPA review and age increment
sections.summary: The CYPA is being reviewed for possible amendments, including incrementing the age to close that gap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The CYPA is being reviewed for a range of possible amendments, including this increment of the age to close that gap.

sections.label: Adult abuse reporting guide
sections.summary: A child abuse reporting guide exists and the same will be done for adult abuse, neglect and self-neglect, but no mandatory scheme will be implemented for now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: As I have said earlier, there is a child abuse reporting guide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will do the same for adult abuse, neglect and self-neglect so as to uplift the capabilities and awareness of all our frontline stakeholders who are nodal points in this important community-based network to look out for vulnerable adults and children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Let us continue to strengthen our partners' awareness and their understanding that this is actually a very important role that they have to play in addition to the primary function, whatever that may be, and let us see if we can identify more cases that might be previously invisible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But as I have said, for now, we are not going to implement a mandatory scheme.

sections.label: Drafted definitions breadth and clarity
sections.summary: The definitions are drafted with sufficient breadth while assuring the community and public that there will be some clear definition to operate on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We want the best of both worlds actually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But I think we have drafted the definitions with sufficient breadth and yet need to assure the community and members of the public that there will be some clear definition that we operate on.
